To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the differential modulatory effects of high maize oil diet, rich in n-6 polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFA), and extra virgin olive oil (EVOO) rich in monounsaturated fatty acids (MUFA) on mammary cancer promotion may be exerted through specific changes in the composition of the membrane of the tumor cells.
dietary lipids modulate breast cancer development in rats, and this is associated with changes in tumor cell membranes.
dietary fat composition modulates the composition of the membrane of mammary tumor cells, which may explain its differential effects during mammary cancer promotion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the effects of different dietary lipids on mammary carcinogenesis, in particular the effects of maize oil and olive oil on mammary carcinomas in rats.
the study of the effects of the dietary lipids on the composition of the membranes of mammary tumor cells.
the study of the effects and mechanisms of action of the dietary fat in the mammary carcinogenesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the differentially modulating effects of the experimental diets in mammary carcinogenesis are, at least partially, mediated through changes in the membrane composition of the tumor cells.

dietary lipids, especially those of olive oil, may modulate the carcinogenic process through changes in the membrane lipid composition and in the membrane proteins, and that the membrane lipid changes are related to the differential effects of the diets on the carcinogenic process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the different effects of the diets on the mammary carcinogenesis are mediated by specific changes in the membrane lipid composition of the tumor cells.
dietary lipids modulate carcinogenesis in the mammary gland through changes in the composition of the cell membrane of the mammary tumor.
dietary lipids, especially those from vegetable oils, can induce specific changes in membrane composition of breast cancer cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the differential effects exerted by maize oil rich diet and virgin olive oil rich diet during mammary carcinogenesis could be exerted through specific changes in the composition of tumor cell membrane, which could lead to different signaling pathways.
dietary lipids can modulate the carcinogenesis process by modifying the composition of the cell membrane.
the dietary lipid composition modulates the membrane composition of breast cancer cells and, consequently, the aggressiveness of the tumor.
